questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there Is no need to substitute It, select ‘No substitution’. We were quite impressed with the enthusiasm that she work for .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there Is no need to substitute It, select ‘No substitution’.

We were quite impressed with the enthusiasm that she work for.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'that she worked with'.

Key Points

  • The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'that she worked with' should be used instead of 'that she work for'.
  • The phrasal verb 'worked for' means 'To be an employee of some person, group, or organization'.
    • Example: I worked for my father for three years before I had enough money to go to college.
  • In the given context, 'worked with' should be used.
  • As the given sentence is in the past tense the verb 'work' will be changed into 'worked'.
  • The phrasal verb 'work with' means 'To cooperate with someone in order to perform some task, activity, responsibility, etc.'
    • Example: You'll be working with Karen on this project.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.
     

Correct Sentence: We were quite impressed with the enthusiasm that she worked with. 

Hinglish

  • दिए गए वाक्य में रेखांकित भाग व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहां, 'that she work for' के बजाय 'that she worked with' का इस्तेमाल किया जाना चाहिए।
  • Phrasal Verb 'worked for' का अर्थ है 'किसी व्यक्ति, समूह या संगठन का कर्मचारी होना'।
    • ​Example: I worked for my father for three years before I had enough money to go to college.
  • दिए गए संदर्भ में 'worked with' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • जैसा कि दिया गया वाक्य भूतकाल में है, क्रिया 'work' को 'worked' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
  • Phrasal Verb 'work with' का अर्थ है 'किसी कार्य, गतिविधि, जिम्मेदारी, आदि को करने के लिए किसी के साथ सहयोग करना'।
    • ​Example: You'll be working with Karen on this project.
  • इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

questions.question: Select the option that will most suitably substitute the underlined part of the given sentence. I gave my best dress to her on condition that she return it the very next day in a clean condition.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will most suitably substitute the underlined part of the given sentence.

I gave my best dress to her on condition that she return it the very next day in a clean condition.

options.text: on the condition that she return
options.html: on the condition that she return

options.text: on the conditions that she had return
options.html: on the conditions that she had return

options.text: on the condition that she would return
options.html: on the condition that she would return

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • The word "condition" means a requirement that must be fulfilled before something else can happen. (शर्त)
    • Example: She agreed to the job offer on the condition that she would receive regular promotions.
  • "Would" is used to indicate a future action or state that is dependent on a condition. (करेंगे/होगा)
    • Example: He said he would help me if I needed it.
  • Hence, the correct substitution is 'on the condition that she would return'.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: on the condition that she return (शर्त पर कि वह लौट आए): This option is grammatically incorrect because the verb form is not in the correct tense.
    • Example: She agreed on the condition that she return the book.
  • Option 2: on the conditions that she had return (शर्तों पर कि उसने वापसी की थी): This option is incorrect due to the misuse of "conditions" and wrong verb tense.
    • Example: He accepted on the conditions that she had return the favor earlier.
  • Option 4: on condition that she returned (शर्त पर कि वह लौट आई): Although this option is grammatically correct, it changes the tense of the original sentence.
    • Example: She agreed on condition that she returned the money.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can replace the bracketed word segment in the following sentence. Classical buildings in ancient Greek and Roman times were (characteristically built) from marble or some other attractive, durable stone.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can replace the bracketed word segment in the following sentence.

Classical buildings in ancient Greek and Roman times were (characteristically built) from marble or some other attractive, durable stone.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The word "characteristically built" means something that is typically constructed in a particular way, often reflecting the defining qualities or features of the time period or style. (विशिष्ट रूप से निर्मित)
    • Example: The houses in this region are characteristically built with sloping roofs to withstand heavy snowfall.
  • "Typically built" refers to the common or usual method of construction, implying that it follows a standard or common pattern. (आम तौर पर निर्मित)
    • Example: Modern skyscrapers are typically built with steel and glass for both strength and aesthetic appeal.
  • Hence, we can infer that "characteristically built" and "typically built" are synonymous in the context of the given sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Fascinating to build (आकर्षक बनाने के लिए): Refers to something that is extremely interesting or delightful to construct.
    • Example: The ancient pyramids would have been fascinating to build with the technology available at the time.
  • Strange build (अजीब निर्माण): Refers to something constructed in an unusual or peculiar manner.
    • Example: The artist's house has a strange build with odd angles and unexpected shapes.
  • Mainly having been built (मुख्य रूप से बनाया गया): Refers to something that was constructed primarily or mostly in a particular way.
    • Example: The ancient city was mainly having been built with mud bricks due to the lack of stone.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. Play cards is not allowed here
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Play cards is not allowed here
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2)

Key Points

  • The word "play" means to engage in an activity for enjoyment and recreation rather than a serious or practical purpose. (खेलना)
    • Example: Children love to play in the park.
  • "Playing cards" refers to the activity of using a set of cards for games, gambling, or magic tricks. (ताश खेलना)
    • Example: Playing cards is a common pastime during family gatherings.

Hence, the phrase 'Playing cards' correctly substitutes the underlined segment in the sentence.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Playing card (ताश का पत्ता): Refers to a single card from a deck used for playing games.
    • Example: He picked a playing card from the deck.
  • Play card (ताश खेलना): Incorrect form for the context of the sentence.
    • Example: Incorrect usage: Play card is not allowed here.
  • Played cards (ताश खेली): Refers to the past action of playing cards.
    • Example: They played cards all night.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. You have tears , prepare to shed them now.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

You have tears, prepare to shed them now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

Key Points

  • The phrase "If you have tears" is used to indicate a conditional situation where someone is expected to have tears. (यदि आपके पास आँसू हैं)
    • Example: If you have tears, let them flow now.
  • "Prepare to shed them now" means to get ready to cry or show emotions immediately. (अब उन्हें बहाने के लिए तैयार हो जाओ)
    • Example: The heartbreaking news made everyone prepare to shed their tears.

Hence, we can infer that the correct phrase is "If you have tears" as it logically fits the context of the sentence.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Yet you have tears (फिर भी आपके पास आँसू हैं): This suggests a contrast or contradiction that is not suitable for the given sentence.
    • Example: Yet you have tears, even though you said you wouldn't cry.
  • Until you have tears (जब तक आपके पास आँसू नहीं आते): This indicates a time condition that doesn't fit the context.
    • Example: Wait here until you have tears in your eyes.
  • Unless you have tears (जब तक आपके पास आँसू नहीं हैं): This implies a condition that must not be met, which is incorrect for the given sentence.
    • Example: You won't understand the pain unless you have tears in your eyes.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. He always used to say that he was not a beggar by choice and if someone could employ him, he would like to eat .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

He always used to say that he was not a beggar by choice and if someone could employ him, he would like to eat.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

Key Points

  • The phrase "employ him, he would like to eat" in the context means he would prefer to work rather than beg for food. (उसे नौकरी मिलेगी, तो वह खाना पसंद करेगा।)
    • Example: If given a chance, he would like to eat what he earns through work.
  • "Love to work" means having a strong liking or enthusiasm for working. (काम करना पसंद करना)
    • Example: She loves to work on challenging projects that push her limits.

Hence, the correct substitution for "he would like to eat" is "love to work".

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Listen to me (मुझे सुनो): To pay attention to what someone is saying.
    • Example: Please listen to me carefully before you make a decision.
  • linger at work (काम पर देर तक रुकना): To stay in a place longer than necessary.
    • Example: He tends to linger at work even after his shift ends.
  • live to work (काम के लिए जीना): To have work as the central focus of one's life.
    • Example: He lives to work and rarely takes vacations.

Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The manager noticed a discrepancy between the two audit reports.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The manager noticed a discrepancy between the two audit reports.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'Major difference."

Key Points

  •  The word 'Discrepancy' itself implies a notable of significant difference between the two audit reports.
    • Example- Discrepancies in the firm's financial statements led to an investigations.
  • 'Major difference' it emphasizes the significance of the two variation observed by the manager, indicating that it is substantial enough to warrant attention.
    • Example- This is the third major difference between the two sets of meetings.
  • Hence, the correct answer is 'Major difference'.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.

Additional Information

  •  The rest of the options are incorrect because;
  • 'Deliberate mistake'- The sentence does not imply any intent behind the difference observed by the manager. It simply states that a difference was noticed.
  • 'Selfish interest' - The manager noticing a discrepancy between audit reports does not necessarily relate to selfish interests. it's more about identifying inconsistences or error on the reports.
  • 'Great similarity'-  The sentence states that the manager noticed a discrepancy, indicating a lack of similarity or agreement between the two audit reports.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I don't know which career he will choose. He delays making strong decisions .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I don't know which career he will choose. He delays making strong decisions.

options.text: is as clean as a whistle
options.html: is as clean as a whistle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

Key Points

  • The idiom "sits on the fence" means to delay making a decision when you have to choose between two sides in an argument or a competition. (निर्णय लेने में देरी करना)
    • Example: When asked whether he supports the new policy, he just sits on the fence and avoids giving a clear answer.

Therefore, the correct statement is "I don't know which career he will choose. He sits on the fence."

Additional InformationHere are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • is as clean as a whistle (बिल्कुल साफ): Used to describe something that is very clean or clear.
    • Example: The kitchen was as clean as a whistle after the thorough cleaning.
  • turns a blind eye (अनदेखा करना): To deliberately ignore something.
    • Example: She turns a blind eye to the mistakes of her favorite employees.
  • spills the beans (रहस्य खोल देना): To reveal secret information.
    • Example: He spilled the beans about the new project ahead of the official announcement.

questions.question: Select the option that can substitute the bracketed word segment meaningfully. Writing can instil a number of emotions (as in a reader).
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can substitute the bracketed word segment meaningfully.

Writing can instil a number of emotions (as in a reader).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

Key Points

  • The word "within" means inside or enclosed in something; it denotes being in the interior of something. (के भीतर)
    • Example: She felt a sense of peace within her heart.
  • "Within a reader" refers to the internal emotional or mental state of a reader, suggesting that writing can evoke emotions inside a reader. (पाठक के भीतर)
    • Example: The story stirred deep emotions within a reader, making them reflect on their own life experiences.

Therefore, the correct answer is: 'Option 1.'

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Instead a reader (इसके बजाय एक पाठक): This phrase is grammatically incorrect and does not convey any meaningful sense.
    • Example: Incorrect usage: Writing can instil a number of emotions instead a reader.
  • Until a reader (जब तक एक पाठक): This phrase suggests a condition or a point in time, which is not applicable in the context of the sentence.
    • Example: Incorrect usage: Writing can instil a number of emotions until a reader.
  • Among a reader (एक पाठक के बीच): This phrase is incorrect as "among" is used for more than one person or thing.
    • Example: Incorrect usage: Writing can instil a number of emotions among a reader.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Her hopes for building her own house were beaten when she lost her jewellery box.

Her hopes for building her own house were beaten when she lost her jewellery box.
questions.solution: "Beaten" in this context indicates "defeated" or "crushed". "Dashed" is slang for "ruined" or "destroyed". The woman's plans to construct her own home were dashed, according to the sentencing, when she misplaced her jewellery box. Option 4 is, thus, the right response.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Shrija enquired about his daughter’s reputation.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Shrija enquired about his daughter’s reputation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "asked about his daughter’s character. "

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meaning of the given words.
    • assessed: 
      evaluate or estimate the nature, ability, or quality of.
    • condemned: 
      sentenced to a particular punishment, especially death.
    • poked: 
      jab or prod (someone or something) with one's finger or a sharp object.
    • asked: 
      say something in order to obtain an answer or some information.
  • As per the meaning of the words, "asked" is the appropriate word for the underlined part of the given sentence.
  • Options 1, 2, and 3 have different meanings from the given sentence.
  • Option 4 has the same meaning as the given sentence.
The correct sentence is: Shrija asked about his daughter’s character.
Hence, the correct answer is option 4.​

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He has recovered now and is feeling too strong to walk .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He has recovered now and is feeling too strong to walk.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • The word "too" means to a higher degree than is desirable, permissible, or possible; excessively. (बहुत)
    • Example: He was too tired to continue the journey.
  • "Strong enough" means having sufficient strength to perform an action. (पर्याप्त मजबूत)
    • Example: She is strong enough to lift the heavy box.

Hence, the phrase should be "strong enough to walk" instead of "too strong to walk".

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: too weak to walk (चलने के लिए बहुत कमजोर): This means not having enough strength to walk.
    • Example: After the illness, he was too weak to walk.
  • Option 2: weak enough to walk (चलने के लिए पर्याप्त कमजोर): This phrase is incorrect as it contradicts itself.

  • Option 4: strong to walk (चलने के लिए मजबूत): This phrase is grammatically incorrect.
    • Example: He is strong enough to walk.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Had I known that you were planning to visit me, I should have done all the necessary arrangements.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Had I known that you were planning to visit me, I should have done all the necessary arrangements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The phrase "I should have made" is grammatically incorrect in this context. (मुझे बनाना चाहिए था)
    • Example: I should have made a reservation earlier.
  • "I would have made" is the correct form here, indicating a conditional past action that did not happen. (मैंने बनाया होता)
    • Example: Had I known about the meeting, I would have made arrangements to attend it.
  • Hence, the correct phrase to use is 'I would have made' instead of 'I should have made'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • I should have made (मुझे बनाना चाहिए था): This phrase implies a sense of obligation or duty that was not fulfilled.
    • Example: I should have made a cake for the party.
  • I would have do (मैंने किया होता): This is grammatically incorrect as "do" should be "done."
    • Example: Incorrect: I would have do it if I had time. Correct: I would have done it if I had time.
  • I must have made (मुझे बनाया होगा): This implies a high degree of certainty about a past action.
    • Example: I must have made a mistake in the calculations.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Many a women work for the betterment of their family.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Many a women work for the betterment of their family.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The phrase "Many a" is used with a singular noun and a singular verb to emphasize the large number of something. (अनेक)
    • Example: Many a student has benefited from this scholarship program.
  • "Woman" refers to an adult female human. (महिला)
    • Example: The woman at the counter was very helpful.
  • Hence, "Many a woman" is the correct phrase to use, and it should be followed by the singular verb "works".

Therefore, the correct answer is: "Many a woman works for".

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 2: Many a women works for (अनेक महिलाएं काम करती हैं): This is incorrect because "Many a" should be followed by a singular noun and verb.
    • Example: Many a women works for the betterment of their family. (Incorrect)
  • Option 3: Many a women working for (अनेक महिलाएं काम कर रही हैं): This is incorrect because it uses the plural noun "women" and changes the verb form.
    • Example: Many a women working for the betterment of their family. (Incorrect)
  • Option 4: Many a woman worked for (अनेक महिलाओं ने काम किया): This is incorrect because it uses the past tense "worked".
    • Example: Many a woman worked for the betterment of their family. (Incorrect)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. There is no place on the bench.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

There is no place on the bench.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2)

Key Points

  • The word "room" means space that can be occupied or where something can be done. (जगह)
    • Example: There is no room for error in this critical project.
  • "no room" refers to the absence of space or capacity. (कोई जगह नहीं)
    • Example: There is no room on the shelf for more books.

Hence, the phrase 'no room' is the most appropriate substitution for 'no place' in the given sentence.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • no life (कोई जीवन नहीं): Absence of living beings or activity.
    • Example: The desert showed no signs of life.
  • more space (अधिक स्थान): Additional area or capacity.
    • Example: We need more space to accommodate all the guests.
  • more place (अधिक जगह): Additional location or area.
    • Example: We need more place to store our belongings.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. Srinu had to take a break from his training for the marathon during the lockdown so he decided to go to his hometown.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

Srinu had to take a break from his training for the marathon during the lockdown so he decided to go to his hometown.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He is almost quiet well.

Key Points

  • The word "quiet" means making little or no noise; being calm and silent. (शांत)
    • Example: The library is a quiet place for reading and studying.
  • "Quite" is an adverb that means completely or to a certain degree; it is used for emphasis. (काफी)
    • Example: She was quite happy with the results of her exam.
  • Hence, in the sentence "He is almost quiet well," the correct word to use is 'quite' to indicate the degree of wellness.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

    • Example: He almost quietly left the room without anyone noticing.
  • Option 2: very quite (बहुत शांत): This phrase is grammatically incorrect as "quite" and "very" should not be used together in this context.
    • Example: The phrase "very quite" is not grammatically correct.
  • Option 4: quiet (शांत): This word means "silent" and does not fit the context of the sentence properly.
    • Example: The room was very quiet after everyone left.

questions.question: Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined phrase in the following sentence. Even though she’s a celebrity, she doesn’t draw any attention towards herself .

questions.question: Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. There was also a (signal fall) in Bandra following the heavy rains.
questions.questionHtml:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

There was also a (signal fall) in Bandra following the heavy rains.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3) i.e. signal failure.
Key Points
  • The original phrase "signal fall" is not a common or standard expression in English.
  • The term "signal failure" is widely used and understood, particularly in the context of infrastructure issues such as those caused by heavy rains disrupting signal systems.
  • "Signal fall" could confuse the reader as it might imply a physical falling of a signal structure, which is not typically what happens during heavy rain. Instead, the issue is a malfunction or disruption.
  • "Signal failure" correctly captures the idea of a disruption in the signal system due to external factors like weather conditions.
Therefore, the correct answer is: signal failure.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. The professor did an objective evaluation.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. In yesterday’s fire accident, her feets are burnt badly.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

In yesterday’s fire accident, her feets are burnt badly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • The word "feet" is the plural form of "foot," which refers to the lower extremity of the leg below the ankle, on which a person stands or walks. (पैर)
    • Example: She dipped her feet in the cool water to relax.
  • "Were" is the past tense plural form of the verb "to be," used with plural subjects. (थे)
    • Example: They were happy with their results.
  • Hence, the correct phrase is "her feet were" to indicate that both feet were affected in the past incident.

Therefore, the correct sentence is "In yesterday’s fire accident, her feet were burnt badly."

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: her feet was (उसके पैर था): Incorrect because "was" is singular and "feet" is plural.
    • Example: Incorrect: Her feet was cold. Correct: Her feet were cold.
  • Option 2: her foots were (उसके पांव थे): Incorrect because "foots" is not the correct plural form of "foot."
    • Example: Incorrect: Her foots were aching. Correct: Her feet were aching.
  • Option 4: No substitution (कोई प्रतिस्थापन नहीं): Incorrect because the original phrase "her feets are" is grammatically incorrect.
    • Example: Incorrect: Her feets are cold. Correct: Her feet were cold.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The library is the right place to write an article from a journal.
